s: Hello and welcome to Word Kitchen!
Let's start with our first word: city.
A city is a big town.
Many people live in a city.
Lena, do you live in a big city?
I live in a big city.
There are cars in the city.
There are shops in the city.
But I grew up in a village.
A village is a very small town.
Few people live in a village.
There are no big shops in my village.
There are trees in my village.
In my city, I go to the library.
A library is a place with many books.
The library in my city is very big.
My village is too small for a library.
A school is a place where children learn.
I went to the village school.
The school was small, but the teachers were great.
In the city, my school is big!
My school has one thousand children.
One thousand children learn at my school.
That is a very big school!
After school, I walk to the library.
I read at the library every day.
When my family visits the city, we sleep in a hotel.
A hotel is a place where you sleep on a trip.
The hotel has a nice bed.
When your family comes to my city, they sleep in the hotel near my home.
The hotel is close to the library.
It is close to my school too.
And from the hotel, we walk in the city.
The city is big, but the hotel is quiet.
My school is close to the library.
I go to the library after school.
The library is my favorite place in the city.
I read at the library with my friends.
I want to see your big school!
And I want to see your library.
My village has no library, so I will take books from your library to my village school.
Maya, when I visit your village, where do I sleep?
Is there a hotel in the village?
No, my village has no hotel.
The village is too small for a hotel.
But you can sleep at my home in the village!
My home in the village is small, but it is warm.
You will like my village home.
So the village is quiet, and the city is loud.
The village has no library, but the school has books.
The city has a big library and a big school.
The city has hotels, but the village has no hotel.
I like the city and the village.
Let's say our five words one more time.
Join us tomorrow on Word Kitchen.
